widgets_values:
Three.js scene, every node in WAS Suite/Three.

Three Viewer draws the scene on the canvas and the camera can be dragged.
Three Render draws the same scene off-screen and hands back an IMAGE batch: 24 frames
of a full turn from the perspective camera, and one frame from the orthographic one. Drag
the strip on Three Render to move the captured window.
Three Compile writes the whole thing out as a zip. Unpack it and serve the folder over a
local web server, then open index.html: the scene runs with no ComfyUI and no network.

Three Render needs a ComfyUI tab open on this canvas while the graph runs. The browser
draws the frames and sends them back.

Three Load Model and the Transform Object beside it are switched off, because the model
menu lists your own files and not this graph's. Pick one, turn both back on with Ctrl-B,
and it joins the scene on the group's eighth slot.


Three Environment lights every physical material from a studio room built in code, which
is what stops polished metal rendering black. Three Bloom and Three Antialias chain into
both apps' effects sockets; an effects chain turns the app's own antialias off, which is
what the antialias node puts back.
Every moving thing here reads the captured window rather than the clock, so the batch
loops: Three Animate Transform on 'per capture', Three Custom Update off ctx.duration,
and the shader off its progress uniform. The turn is 345 degrees over 24 frames, not 360,
so the last frame does not repeat the first. For n frames it is 360 * (n - 1) / n.
